meeting_point: Samuel Adams statue in front of Faneuil Hall
location_address: Samuel Adams Statue in front of Faneuil Hall Boston, MA US 02109
accessibility: Stroller and wheelchair accessible. Terrain: mostly flat surfaces and little to no inclines
description:
This private tour is the perfect introduction to Boston’s Revolutionary history! Visit some of the key sites along the world-famous Freedom Trail in this engaging, one-hour guided walking tour.  

Journey into the past as you hear stories about events that took place in the Old State House, Faneuil Hall, King’s Chapel and the Old South Meeting House. Learn about the diverse people, places and events that started a revolution.

The people of colonial Boston were ordinary people.  Shaped by the times that they lived in, they rose to the cause, and achieved extraordinary things!

*Private tours are bookable online for groups of up to 20 people with at least 1 week's notice. To request a private tour for groups of more than 20 people use the Private Tour Request form. Please provide at least 1-2 weeks notice in advance of your preferred tour date for larger groups.* [Private tour request form link](https://form.jotform.com/220595239082054)

what_is_included_items.value: Guided 60 minute outdoor introduction to the American Revolution
0.5 mile tour at a moderate pace, stoping at various sites along the tour

what_is_not_included: - This tour includes stops at select stops along the Freedom Trail. It does not include the entire 2.5 mile Freedom Trail. If you are interested in a more in-depth American Revolution tour, our 2hr Road to Revolution tour includes stops in both downtown Boston and the North End neighborhood.
